clue.text: Being full of years guarantees pain unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters of guarantees pain are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A promise that pain lies ahead, the gloomy lot of someone growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the fourteen letters of GUARANTEES PAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in their seventies has lived many years, which is what full of years conveys.

clue.text: What an heir expects to do is to prosper

definitions.text: What an heir expects to do

explanation.surface: An heir's expectations are a kind of hope to flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir follows on to a title or estate; to do well or thrive is the other sense of the same verb.

clue.text: It could help a writer get to the point

definitions.text: It could help a writer get to the point

parts.words: It could help a writer get to the point
parts.note: reads like advice on concise prose, but means a gadget that gives a pencil a sharp tip

explanation.surface: Something that helps an author stop waffling and come to the matter at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil user needs a sharp tip, and this device grinds the wood and lead into one.

clue.text: One international organisation needing to get with it

parts.note: UN is the ... Nations, an international body
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single global body having to get up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, a whole counted as one.

clue.text: Private Ben meets the queen

parts.note: Ben Gunn is the marooned castaway in Stevenson's Treasure Island
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A soldier called Ben is presented to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the crossword convention for the Queen. A gunner is the rank of private in the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British artillery the lowest rank of soldier is called a gunner, equivalent to a private.

clue.text: Film bring us spun version of recent events?

definitions.text: Film bring us spun version of recent events?

parts.words: Film bring us spun version of recent events?
parts.note: suggests a propaganda film with a slanted account, but describes reels of film that are wound on and show the latest happenings

explanation.surface: A cinema piece offering a biased take on the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spun' hints at political spin, but a reel of film is literally spun through a projector; recent events are news.
explanation.definitionFit: Before television, cinemas screened short films reporting current affairs, the source of the nation's moving-picture news.

clue.text: Religious instruction for a group that's wild and noisy

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a school subject
pro means in favour of, so for
a ring is a group, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: Scripture lessons for a gang of rowdy pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: RI (religious instruction) was the old name for RE lessons in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Rip-roaring describes boisterous, uproarious behaviour, rowdy and loud.

clue.text: Piece of drama that's laughably incompetent?

definitions.text: Piece of drama that's laughably incompetent?

parts.words: Piece of drama that's laughably incompetent?
parts.note: reads as a scathing review of a bad production, but names a Shakespeare play whose title describes a farce of mistakes

explanation.surface: A theatre critic's dismissal of a hopelessly bungled play.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, a funny sequence of blunders is what the title of Shakespeare's early comedy of mistaken twins says.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's farce of two sets of twins is a stage play, and its title literally means a funny series of mistakes.

clue.text: Unemotional saint humming

parts.note: humming is British slang for smelling bad, and olid is an old word for foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A holy figure placidly humming a tune without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humming' looks like a tune, but in British slang to hum is to stink; OLID means rank-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person shows little feeling and is impassive and calm.

clue.text: Commit prisoner and put commitment on paper

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
to sign is to write your name to bind yourself to an agreement

explanation.surface: Sending an inmate away and putting a pledge into writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign is to hand over or deliver, as when someone is committed to prison or the grave.

clue.text: Why look sulky, do you say? Complete disaster

indicators.note: do you say asks how the words sound when spoken, signalling a soundalike

parts.note: to look sulky is to pout, so the phrase gives why pout

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a person is sulking after a total catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A wipeout is a total failure or rout, slang for a crushing defeat.

clue.text: Chieftain to be married in Ireland shortly

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for married goes inside the shortened name for Ireland
shortly means the name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A clan leader is due to wed in Ireland soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims EIRE to EIR; 'in' places M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or commander, a chieftain in the Arab world.

clue.text: Unfortunately we enrolled a good-for-nothing

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests a mishap, so the letters of we enrolled are scrambled

explanation.surface: A school regrets admitting a layabout.
explanation.definitionFit: A ne'er-do-well is a feckless idle person, a wastrel worth nothing.

clue.text: Somewhere like London is made primarily for profit-making system

parts.note: London is an example of a capital city

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of made is used

explanation.surface: London has been built chiefly for commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitalism is the economic system based on private ownership and trading for gain.

clue.text: When cuddled by boy the wrong way is maiden gloomy?

indicators.note: cuddled by means held within the arms of something, so these letters sit inside
the wrong way means the word for boy is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
taken as written
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl hugged clumsily by a young man ends up sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' reverses the boy to make DAL, which 'cuddled by' wraps round IS M. A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal means dreary and depressing, much like low-spirited.

clue.text: Let down with bad debt across the new year

indicators.note: across means the first jumble spans the second, enclosing it
bad means the word debt is mangled into a different order
new means the word year is given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Disappointed by a growing debt over the New Year period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' and 'new' each scramble a word separately (to BETD and RAYE); 'across' has the first spanning the second. Both together hold exactly the letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray someone is to be disloyal and fail them, to let them down.

clue.text: Solid dot to highlight item in report

parts.note: a bullet is the solid dot that marks each item in a list
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for marking a key point in a written report.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official statement or news report.

clue.text: Metal from a can that's got into fruit

indicators.note: got into says these letters have found their way inside the fruit

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Metal from a tin that has ended up inside some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got into' looks like eating, but signals a container: the can goes inside the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious silvery-white chemical element.

clue.text: Explosive device found by dog maybe on a road

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: A bomb found by a dog sniffing along a street.
explanation.walkthrough: A petard is the small bomb of 'hoist with his own petard'.
explanation.definitionFit: A petard was a small bomb used to blow open gates or walls.

clue.text: King wants foul fiend stabbed

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: foul suggests something corrupted, so the letters of fiend are muddled

explanation.surface: A monarch wishes an evil demon put to the dagger.
explanation.definitionFit: To knife someone is to stab them with a blade.

clue.text: Soldier turning up in female garb to deviate

indicators.note: in says the soldier is placed inside the item of clothing

parts.note: a dress is a woman's garment

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier appearing in women's clothing to wander off.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' means reading upwards, so the soldier becomes IG before 'in' places it within the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to stray from the main subject, to wander off the point.

clue.text: Make necessary hospital department — ailments mostly gone

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department; the run of letters across department ailments is a coincidence, not a hidden word

indicators.note: mostly gone means most of the word ailments is dropped, leaving its start

explanation.surface: A hospital ward where most illnesses have been cured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly gone' removes MENTS from AILMENTS, leaving AIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve as an unavoidable consequence, to require.

clue.text: Sail to Portugal? That's brave

parts.note: taken as written
P is the international vehicle registration letter for Portugal
gallant means brave

explanation.surface: Is sailing to Portugal a courageous act?
explanation.definitionFit: A topgallant is a sail set above the topsail on a square-rigged ship.

clue.text: Puritan quietly getting the gear

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction meaning quietly
rig means equipment or gear

explanation.surface: A strict moralist quietly buying the kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A prig is a self-righteous person with a priggish moral strictness.

clue.text: Fan beginning to gloat after victory

indicators.note: after places the letter from gloat behind the word for victory

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of gloat is taken

explanation.surface: A supporter starting to crow after the team triumphs.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing is a flap or vane, and a fan blade is likewise a wing that moves air.

clue.text: Turn funny having drunk port and act without restraint

indicators.note: having drunk means taking something inside, so the port goes within
funny means odd, so the letters of turn are rearranged

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Someone goes odd after downing port and behaves wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' scrambles the first word into RUNT; 'having drunk' means it swallows the Brazilian port.
explanation.definitionFit: To run riot is to behave in a wild, uncontrolled way.

clue.text: 'Fatty is a dope' — that's cruel!

indicators.note: cruel suggests rough treatment, so the letters of is a dope are knocked about

explanation.surface: Calling someone fat and stupid is an unkind insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose describes body fat, as in adipose tissue.

clue.text: Experts helping police to sort minor logistics out

indicators.note: sort, read with the out that follows the fodder as the phrasal verb sort out, means reorganise, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the words minor logistics supply the letters; the trailing out only completes the phrasal verb sort out

explanation.surface: Forensic specialists aiding detectives to organise small practical matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort ... out' rearranges MINOR LOGISTICS; the out completes the phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: These specialists study crime and offenders and advise detectives.
